# Super Hang-On Enhanced 2.1

The build applies `enhanced.patch` to [jotego/jtcores at 8bc8172](https://github.com/jotego/jtcores/tree/8bc8172993b9b9488cb45ee8a913090fc4d9b143). All six MRA definitions come from [jotego/jtbin at d2274ea](https://github.com/jotego/jtbin/tree/d2274ea43a04af815ef987291aa385abe5324372/mra). `MRA-SHA256SUMS` records the original bytes before packaging. The package changes only each MRA's RBF reference. It contains no game ROMs.

The [official MiSTer build for shanon](https://github.com/jotego/jtcores/actions/runs/45348334385/job/138288661207) ran `xjtcore.sh shanon mister pocket` against the digest `jotego/jtcore20@sha256:a0397645aeac483f90718c89e5fd491c4889db6e4202bcba7f7f7770e14beb6b` at official commit `19859e88e5a41cabf8abf3e30ae3a137c9561df6`. The public log identifies this image. The candidate uses the same digest and checks the running compiler for Quartus Prime Lite 20.1.1 Build 720. The candidate also requires nonnegative setup, hold, recovery, removal and minimum pulse width margins before packaging.

The original cabinet uses steering, accelerate, brake and Supercharger. The first three button slots in the original MRAs are Accelerate, Brake and Supercharger. The fourth slot is blank. USB Start and Coin depend on the complete four-slot layout. SNAC can program each of the three digital actions with three Start taps while holding that action. Repeating the gesture removes it. Each action starts in manual mode. Native analog axes still feed the game's ADC in analog stick, trigger and wheel configurations. A pressed digital pedal overrides its own ADC channel. When that button is released, the game reads the native analog sample again.

`simulate.sh` generates the effective menu and definitions, then tests the production serial input module against the actual cabinet registers in the SHANON variant of `jtoutrun_main`. It covers all 256 steering codes, all three control profiles, Start, Coin, the reserved slot, USB fallback, all six SNAC modes, deliberate activation, deactivation and release. NES and PC Engine provide two digital action buttons. The shared regressions also cover pause credits, Controller Guide and the Gamer-Pro/BlisSTer protocol. Physical controls must be verified on a MiSTer with this build.
